title: Solicitation Notice for Indefinite Delivery Contract (IDC) for Regional Dredge Multiple Award Task Order (MATOC) - USACE Huntington District - W91237-27-R-A003
description: 1. CONTRACT INFORMATION: The contract consists of a base period of one-year with four option periods, one-year each for maintenance dredging and/or clearing and snagging services for Ohio River Government Lock facilities and Ohio River open channel areas (within commercial navigation limits) located in the geographical boundaries of the following U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Great Lakes and Ohio River Division Districts: Nashville (LRN), Louisville (LRL), Huntington (LRH), and Pittsburgh (LRP). There will be no site visit for this requirement. The award of a target of (3) Firm Fixed price Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (IDIQ-MATOC) is anticipated. The contracts will be awarded to up to three (3) qualifying Offerors. The total capacity for the sum of all task orders issued under these contracts is a shared Not to Exceed (NTE) amount of $45,000,000.00. This announcement is open to all businesses regardless of size. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990, which has a size standard of $37 million in average annual receipts. If a large business is awarded this contract, it must comply with RFO Clause 52.219-9 Alt II Small Business Subcontracting Plan, Alternate II. Solicitation documents will be available on or about November 10, 2026, and can be downloaded at https://www.sam.gov. 2. PROJECT INFORMATION: The primary objective of this contract is to provide maintenance dredging and/or clearing and snagging services for Ohio River Government lock facilities and Ohio River open channel areas (within commercial navigation limits) located anywhere within the geographical boundaries of the following Great Lakes and Ohio River Division Districts: Nashville (LRN), Louisville (LRL), Huntington (LRH), and Pittsburgh (LRP). This includes work on any navigable tributary of the Ohio River system.3. SELECTION CRITERIA: All proposals will be evaluated on the basis of the factors stated below to award a contract to each and all qualifying offerors. There will be no trade-offs performed. Awards of MATOCs will be made to those offerors that are determined to be a responsible source, submitting a technically acceptable proposal that conforms to the requirements of the solicitation, and the Contracting Officer has no reason to believe would be likely to offer other than fair and reasonable pricing. FACTOR 1: Technical Capability - This factor evaluates the offerors proposed capability to perform specific dredging and related tasks that may be required under the basic contract and all option periods. FACTOR 2: Equipment - Offeror shall provide documentation for all marine floating plant/equipment being proposed for use under this solicitation/contract and any subsequent task orders. FACTOR 3: Past Performance - Provide descriptions of at least one (1) and no more than three (3) projects completed or substantially complete (90% or more) within seven (7) years from issuance of the solicitation that are similar in scope, magnitude, and complexity to the work under this MATOC. Self-performance of at least 50% of the total cost of the project is required. FACTOR 4: Small Business Participation Plan - This factor evaluates the offerors proposed level of participation of Small Business (as prime and/or subcontractor) relative to the following goals: Small Business (SB) - minimum mandatory (23%), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) (13%), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) (5%), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) (5%), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) (5%), and HUBZone Small Business (3%).4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Proposers shall submit all documents electronically through PIEE Solicitation Module at www.piee.eb.mil. No paper copies, CD, DVD, thumb drives, email, or facsimile will be accepted. To be eligible for award, a firm must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM). Register via the SAM internet site at www. SAM.gov. Questions may be submitted to Amy L. Davis; amy.l.davis@usace.army.mil. Please note, as of April 2018, GSAs System for Award Management (SAM) system requires new registrations and renewals of existing registrations to submit an original signed notarized letter identifying the authorized Entity Administrator. The notarized letter is not to be submitted to the Huntington Contracting Office as it is not our requirement. Vendors are encouraged to check their entitys status in www.SAM.gov and plan accordingly. If the prospective contractor is not registered in the SAM database, the Contracting Officer will follow the procedures in FAR 4.1103. Contact the supporting Federal Service Desk at www.fsd.gov, or by telephone at 866-606-8220 (toll free) or 334-206-7828 (internationally) Monday through Friday from 8am to 8pm EDT, for free assistance. The SAM registration process may take several weeks to process once submitted. Please carefully consider this information when deciding to submit your proposal. ***The Government has determined consolidation is necessary and justified. A redacted version of the approved determination will be posted with the solicitation.

R--Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator Code
description: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a presolicitation notice for a requirement entitled, �Technical Support for the Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator (PARCS) Code Suite� The objective of this acquisition is to obtain regulatory technical support for the maintenance, code support, assessment, continued development, and user training of the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS code suite, including the interfaces between PARCS and RELAP, TRACE, and SNAP. These activities ensure that the PARCS code suite remains a reliable and modern tool for confirmatory reactor physics and systems analysis. PARCS supports independent regulatory decision making by enabling NRC staff to perform confirmatory evaluations of operator actions, core designs, power uprates, advanced reactor concepts, and license amendment requests. Maintaining and advancing the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS capability is essential for enabling high quality staff reviews under 10 CFR Parts 50 and 52. At a high level, this acquisition will: � Maintain and support the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS code suite, including version control, regression testing, documentation upkeep, bug identification, and corrective maintenance. � Develop and evaluate new code functionality, models, numerical methods, and interfaces needed to support emerging regulatory needs, advanced reactor designs, and new cross section methodologies. � Provide confirmatory analysis support, including model development, coupled system assessments, technical consultation, and code user guidance for NRC staff and program offices. � Deliver training and knowledge transfer activities to ensure NRC staff and authorized users can effectively apply PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS for regulatory analyses. The period of performance is five years with a 1-year base period and four 1-year optional periods. Closing date for receipt of proposals will be on, or about, 30 days thereafter. RFP No. 31310027R00035 will be distributed solely through www.sam.gov. title: SI-Assisted Omni Channel Experience - Request for Information
description: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) operates one of the largest contact center ecosystems in the federal government, serving people with Medicare, ACA Marketplace consumers, and caregivers across phone, chat, web, email, and mail channels. CMS is conducting market research to inform a potential future acquisition for SI-assisted omni channel experience capabilities. This updated RFI builds on an initial market research round (Notice ID 269999, February 2026), its scope is being expanded to include the ACA Marketplace, and incorporates findings from commercial payer benchmarking, vendor landscape analysis, and an internal Discovery Sprint process. This RFI is issued solely for market research and information purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, a commitment to issue a solicitation, or an obligation to award a contract. No proposals are being requested or accepted in response to this RFI. CMS will not pay for information provided in response to this RFI. This RFI serves three purposes: Validate and deepen vendor capability data. This RFI continues market research, building on information received from the previous RFI (Notice ID 269999, February 2026) and incorporating findings from commercial payer benchmarking and vendor landscape analysis. CMS is seeking evidence-based updates on vendor capabilities, pricing models, implementation approaches, governance and evaluation frameworks, and workforce transition approaches. CMS is particularly interested in responses that demonstrate sustained, production-validated performance, not launch-period projections. Surface evidence that resolves CMS's open Discovery Sprint questions, including the boundary between SI-assisted and human-required interactions, the evaluation and go/no-go criteria for scaling pilots to production, and the workforce transition and change management approaches required as containment increases. These questions are detailed in Section 5. Inform a defined downstream process. Vendor responses will directly feed the CMS Discovery Sprint, a structured four-week internal process, and the subsequent acquisition strategy. Responses will not be evaluated as proposals and do not obligate CMS to any acquisition path. Please see attached RFI document and Vendor Response Spreadsheet. Deadline: Responses must be submitted by January 5, 2027 at 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Submission Method: Vendors must submit responses by uploading their files to the designated CMS Box folder: https://cmsbox.app.box.com/f/2aa029c164ae47509a35879ffde9e2c3 Email submissions will not be accepted. Response Format � Questions: Vendors must submit their responses to the questions in Sections 2 through 6 using the RFI Vendor Response Spreadsheet provided with this RFI. Enter each response in the row and column assigned to that question. Do not retype questions into a narrative document in place of completing the spreadsheet. Supplemental Documents (Optional): Vendors may also upload supplemental documents to provide additional context, evidence, or supporting detail beyond what the spreadsheet captures. Supplemental documents are optional and limited to 40 pages combined, excluding organizational charts, and appendices containing production performance data. Supplemental Document Format: PDF or Microsoft Word. Font: Times New Roman or Arial, 11-point minimum. Margins: 1 inch minimum. Organization RFI Vendor Response Spreadsheet (completed, covering base question responses to Sections 2 through 6) Supplemental documents, if submitted, organized to mirror the section structure of this RFI, with each supplemental response clearly identifying the question number it addresses (e.g., TECH-1, SPRINT-5). For Section 5, respondents may answer all questions or select the subset most relevant to their proposed solution � please indicate which questions you are not answering and why. Appendices, if applicable: production performance data, system architecture diagrams, sample reports, and other supporting materials

Surface evidence that resolves CMS's open Discovery Sprint questions, including the boundary between SI-assisted and human-required interactions, the evaluation and go/no-go criteria for scaling pilots to production, and the workforce transition and change management approaches required as containment increases. These questions are detailed in Section 5. Inform a defined downstream process. Vendor responses will directly feed the CMS Discovery Sprint, a structured four-week internal process, and the subsequent acquisition strategy. Responses will not be evaluated as proposals and do not obligate CMS to any acquisition path. Please see attached RFI document and Vendor Response Spreadsheet. Submission Method: Vendors must submit responses by uploading their files to the designated CMS Box folder: https://cmsbox.app.box.com/f/2aa029c164ae47509a35879ffde9e2c3 Email submissions will not be accepted. description: This is a PRESOLICITATION NOTICE for the upcoming Solicitation 75H70127R00002 Zuni Comprehensive Community Health Center (ZCCHC) Cooling Tower Repair by Replacement, located in Zuni, NM. These construction services will be in support of the Indian Health Service (IHS) prepared in accordance with FAR Part 36. The Government anticipates releasing the solicitation on or about December 01, 2026 and will remain open for approximately 30 calendar days. A full scope of work, plans and specifications and Construction Wage Determination will be included in the solicitation documents. Additional details can be found in the solicitation when it is posted to https://sam.gov. SCOPE OF WORK: The purpose of this project is the removal and replacement of the existing cooling tower and cooling basin, along with all associated mechanical, electrical, structural, and control components necessary to deliver a complete, fully operational, and integrated condenser water system including all accessories, modifications, and incidental work for proper operation, safety and code compliance. The new installation shall meet or exceed current performance, reliability, and code requirements. LOCATION OF PROJECT: All work shall be performed at the Zuni Comprehensive Community Health Center, 12 B Ave., Zuni, New Mexico 87327. TERO: TERO fees do apply. (More information will be released in solicitation, but the TERO/Taxation & Revenue office phone number is 505-782-7111) CONSTRUCTION DURATION: Period of Performance is 240 calendar days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $250,000.00 and $500,000.00. SITE VISIT: Details regarding the Site Visit will be included in the solicitation. NOTE: ALL DATES ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE. SEE SOLICITATION FOR OFFICIAL DATES, TIMES, AND LOCATIONS OF SITE VISITS AND DEADLINES. CONTRACT TYPE: The Indian Health Service intends to award a single Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract in support of this requirement. This solicitation will be procured as a Request for Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Part 36 procedures with Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation criteria. This project will be solicited as 100% set aside for Small Businesses under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 238220 Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors. The associated size standard for this procurement is $19.0 million. For information concerning NAICS and SBA size standards, go to http://www.sba.gov. For the purposes of this procurement, a concern is considered a small business if its average annual revenue for the last five (5) years is less than $45.0 million. For information concerning NAICS and SBA size standards, go to http://www.sba.gov. Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database is mandatory to be considered for award. Offerors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the internet at: https://sam.gov. Contractors are encouraged to complete SAM registration as soon as possible; the Government may not delay award for the purpose of allowing a contractor additional time to register in SAM. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check https://sam.gov frequently for any amendments or changes to the solicitation. Hard copy documents will NOT be available � all documents for proposal purposes will be posted at the website for download by interested parties. This notice is for informational purposes only and is NOT a request for submission of offers. No other information is available until issuance of the solicitation itself. No bidder list is maintained. Interested bidders should follow this solicitation notice on https://sam.gov to receive email notifications of any updates to the initial notice including any subsequent amendments. No additional information is available other than what is noted herein. Firms are instructed not to call requesting more information.

Background: Under the authority of Section 104 of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) or Super fund of 1980, as amended by the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA); Subtitle I of the Resource Conservation and Recover y Act (RCRA) and pursuant to the National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan (NCP) (40 CFR Part 300); and in accordance with any reauthorizations or amendment s to any of the above named statutes and new response legislation, the EPA has been delegated the responsibility to undertake response actions with respect to the release or threat of release of hazardous substances, or pollutants and contaminants, that pose an actual or potential threat to human health or welfare, or to the environment. b. Navajo Area Uranium Mines (USEPA Region 9) The Navajo Nation encompasses more than 27,000 square miles, spread amongst the Four Corners Region of the USA (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Arizona). The unique geology of the region makes the Navajo Nation rich in uranium, a radioactive ore in high demand after the development of atomic power and weapons at the close of World War II in the 1940s. Approximately four million tons of uranium ore were extracted during mining operations within the Navajo Nation from 1944 to 1986. Many Navajo people worked the mines, often living and raising families in close proximity to the mines and mills. Uranium mining and milling activities no longer occur on Navajo lands, but the legacy of these activities remains, including more than 500 abandoned uranium mine claims with thousands of mine features such as pits, trenches, holes, etc., and homes and drinking water sources with elevated levels of uranium, radium and other radionuclides. Uranium and other elements (selenium, arsenic, etc.) associated with mine and mill sites also occur naturally at elevated levels in rock, soil, surface water, and groundwater across the Navajo Nation and the broader Four Corners region. USEPA maintains a strong partnership with the Navajo Nation and, since 1994, the USEPA Superfund Program has provided technical assistance and funding to assess potentially contaminated sites and develop a response. In August 2007, the USEPA Superfund Program compiled a Comprehensive Database and Atlas of all known uranium mines on the Navajo Nation. In October 2007, at the request of the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, EPA, along with the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Indian Health Service (IHS) developed a coordinated https://www.epa.gov/navajo-nation-uranium-cleanup to address uranium contamination in consultation with Navajo Nation EPA. d. Region 9 The primary hazardous substance on all the sites referenced in the requirement�s Statement of Work (SOW) is radiological mine and mine related waste; therefore, a significant knowledge base of radiological material handling, environmental data interpretation, and data collection will be required to perform the activities within this SOW. The terrain to access site locations is rough, water is scarce, and the weather is often extreme in most areas. The trails and/or roads to the sites are not improved or maintained. To reach the site locations, 4-wheel drive vehicles (capable of drives over rough dirt/rocky roads) and/or hiking long distances is required. Roads can become impassable in wet weather, and conditions can change quickly. In summer, the conditions are hot and dry; in winter, elevations make them subject to severe cold and high winds. Due to the quick changes in the weather, be aware of the danger of flash floods. While this danger is greatest during the summer monsoon season (July through September), flash floods can occur at any time of the year. e. Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of the Navajo Area Abandoned Mines Response and Construction Services (AMRCS) contract is to provide cleanup, response, and construction services to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), primarily at former uranium mining-related sites on or within the Navajo Nation (within EPA Region 9 in Arizona and New Mexico). 7. title: Germany – Installation of doors – Bildungscampus Naumburg, Schönburger Straße, 06618 Naumburg, Los 3-13A Innentüren Alu-Glas Brandschutz TO Schule
description: Der Burgenlandkreis als Bauherr beabsichtigt die Errichtung eines neuen Schulcampus auf dem Areal „ Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße “, bestehend aus Schulgebäude und 3 - Felder - Sporthalle. Das ebenfalls auf dem Gelände geplante Zentrum für das Berufsvorbereitende Jahr ( BVJ ) ist nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. Das Baufeld für den geplanten Campusneubau befindet sich östlich des Naumburger Zentrums im Geltungsbereich eines rechtsgültigen Bebauungsplanes ( B - Plan Nr . 62 “ Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße" ). Die ehemalige Bebauung sowie die Oberflächenbeläge wurden bereits zurückgebaut. Das Schulgrundstück selbst liegt an der südlich verlaufenden Schönburger Straße sowie an der östlich verlaufenden, im Zuge des B- Plan- Verfahrens neu geplanten und errichteten Dr. - Wilhelm- Kniest- Straße zwischen der Schönburger Straße und der Grochlitzer Straße an. Zum Campus gehört noch das Grundstück mit der Flurstücksnummer 692. Das Straßenquartier zwischen Schönburger- , Rosa-Luxemburg und Grochlitzer Straße ist gekennzeichnet durch eine weitgehend homogen wirkende Bebauung durch meist dreigeschossige Wohngebäude. Das Grundstück ist weitgehend eben und umfasst eine Fläche von 25.196m2. Die baulichen Anlagen des neuen Schulcampus werden auf drei Gebäudebereiche verteilt . In der Angebotsaufforderung sind die Gebäudeteile des Bauvorhabens wie folgt bezeichnet: Teilobjekt A Schulgebäude Das Gebäude, d as die Schulräume der Förderschule, d er Sekundarschule und Teile des BVJ beherbergt, bildet als größte Baumasse das Zentrum der Anlage und ist selbst in drei „ Gebäudekuben“ gegliedert, höhenmäßig gestaffelt zwischen zwei und vier Obergeschossen. D ie drei Baukörperbereiche sind jeweils um einen Innenhofkern gegliedert. Die Gebäude werden in Massivbauweise mit tragenden Wänden und Stützen aus Stahlbeton sowie Stahlbetondecken mit Flachdach errichtet. Die Gründung erfolgt auf Stahlbetonbodenplatten . Der mittlere Gebäudeteil ( A 1) ist unterkellert, d ie nördlichen und südlichen Gebäudeteile ( A2 und A3 ) sind nicht unterkellert. Teilobjekt B Sporthalle Die Drei -Feld-Sporthalle ist im Anschluss an das Schulgebäude nördlich angeordnet . An dem großen Hallenraum mit DIN- Maßen ( 4 5 x 2 7 m ) schließt sich an der südlichen Längsseite ein zweigeschossiger Funktionstrakt an. Die Gebäudegründung für den Sozialtrakt erfolgt als Plattengründung mit bewehrten Stahlbeton- Bodenplatten, die Halle wird mit Einzelfundamenten und Fundamentstreifen unter den Außenwänden gegründet. Die tragenden Wände, Stützen sowie die Geschossdecken im Sozialtrakt werden in Stahlbetonbauweise errichtet. Das Hallendach wird mit Leimholzbindern und einer Tragschale aus Stahltrapezblech ausgebildet. Werkstattgebäude des BVJ (Bauteil C) nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung

buyer: Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Tourismus, Landwirtschaft und Forsten des Landes Sachsen-Anhalt
title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Modernisierung der Überbetrieblichen Ausbildungsstätte der Landesanstalt für Landwirtschaft und Gartenbau Sachsen-Anhalt in Iden - Kanäle der drei Gebäude in eine Sammelgrube zum Abpumpen Rindergülle
description: Das Land Sachsen- Anhalt beabsichtigt für die LLG Iden (Landesanstalt für Landwirtschaft und Gartenbau Sachsen- Anhalt) die Modernisierung der überbetrieblichen Ausbildungsstätte (im Folgenden "ÜBS"), als ankerkannte und über- regional wirksame Bildungseinrichtung mit Vorbildfunktion für die Landwirtschaft. Im Zuge dessen wird der Bereich der Milchvieh- und Rinderhaltung neu errichtet und ausgebaut. Ziel ist die Schaffung einer modernen und zukunftsorientier- ten Milchviehhaltung als Grundlage für Ausbildung, Forschung und Demonstration. Kernbestandteil der Stallanlage ist der technologische Prozess der Milchgewinnung einschließlich der zugehörigen Melktechnik. In diesem Zusammen- hang werden sowohl das automatische als auch das konventionelle Melkverfahren vermittelt. Darüber hinaus umfasst die Ausbildung Themen wie Tierbehandlung, Tierbeurteilung, Klauenpflege, der Umgang mit Kühen mit besonderen Anforderungen (Special-Needs-Kühe) sowie die Fütterung in Theorie und Praxis. Die maximale Gruppengröße der Ausbildungskurse beträgt 12 Auszubildende bei Betreuung durch 1 bis 2 Ausbilder. Zur praktischen Ausbildung gehört der Inhalt der Handhabung der Rindergülle in den Stallgebäuden vom Ort des An- falls über den Transport unterhalb der Stallböden bis zum Abpumpen aus einer zentralen Sammelgrube in externe La- gerbehälter. Die erforderlichen Arbeitsgänge, Kontrolltätigkeiten und Dokumentationspflichten müssen unter Gesichts- punkten der gesetzlichen Rahmenbedingungen gelehrt und nachvollziehbar demonstriert werden. Automatisierte Sys- teme sollen eingesetzt werden, soweit sie Zeit und Arbeitsaufwand sparen ohne die menschliche Kontrolle zu ersetzen. Fernüberwachung der Anlagen sind nicht geplant. Die technischen Anlagen sind entsprechend dem Stand der Technik zuverlässig, langlebig und wartungsfreundlich sowie im Sinne des Umwelt- und Klimaschutzes auszulegen. Der Arbeitssicherheit kommt insbesondere im Hinblick auf die Nutzung als Ausbildungsstätte eine besondere Bedeutung zu. Die anfallende Rindergülle gelangt aus den Stallbereichen der drei Ställe über Spaltenböden oder Entmistungsschieber kontinuierlich bzw. zeitlich gesteuert in Güllekanäle aus Stahlbeton. Angeboten werden soll die technische Ausrüstung zum Homogenisieren dieser Gülle in den Unterflur- Kanälen und in der Sammelgrube über ein Zirkulationssystem sowie die Technik zum Abpumpen der aufgerührten Flüssigkeit aus dieser Sammelgrube. Die Grenze der ausgeschriebenen Leistung bildet das Ende einer Gülle- Druckleitung, das 1 m aus der Vorgrube her - aus Richtung Lagerbehälter geführt wird. Eine Biogasanlage wird derzeit nicht betrieben. Auf Grundlage der vorliegenden Funktionalen Leistungsbeschreibung soll ein voll funktionstüchtiges Unterflur- Güllemanagement- System für die drei Stallgebäude mit allen notwendigen technischen Ausrüstungen entsprechend obigen und untenstehenden Beschreibungen beschafft werden.
